(Surah 35: The Angels, Makkan, and its verses are forty-five.)

In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

﴿All praise is due to God, Originator of the heavens and the earth,﴾ the one who brought them into being. (Fatr) is taken in the sense of splitting, as if He split non-existence by bringing the two out of it. The idafa (construction) here is genuine (mahdah), because the word carries the meaning of the past tense.

﴿who made the angels messengers﴾ intermediaries between God and His prophets and the righteous among His servants, who convey to them His messages through revelation, inspiration and true dreams; or intermediaries between Him and His creation, who convey to them the traces of His workmanship.

﴿with wings, two, three, or four.﴾ Possessors of multiple wings, varying according to the differences in their ranks, by means of which they descend and ascend, or hasten toward that over which God has entrusted them, so that they carry out their charge as He commands. Perhaps He did not intend by this the specific number and the negation of anything beyond it, because it is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Jibril on the night of the Mi'raj and he had six hundred wings.

﴿He adds to creation what He wills.﴾ This is a resumed statement (isti'naf) to indicate that their variation in this respect follows from His will and the requirement of His wisdom, not a matter demanded by their essences. For if the difference in kinds and species, through their distinctive properties and differentia, were due to their shared essences, it would necessitate the contradiction of the properties of things that are alike, which is impossible. The verse encompasses increases in forms and meanings, such as beauty of face, sweetness of voice, soundness of intellect and generosity of soul.

﴿Indeed God is over all things Powerful.﴾ The specification of some things for attainment over others is only from the aspect of will.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 2:

﴿Whatever Allah opens to people of mercy﴾ — i.e., whatever He releases and sends forth to them. This is a metonymy (tajawwuz) of the cause for the effect (majaz mursal, from the cause to the thing caused). ﴿of mercy﴾ — such as blessing, security, health, knowledge, and prophethood. ﴿there is none to withhold it﴾ — none who restrains it. ﴿And whatever He withholds, there is none to release it after Him﴾ — none who sets it free. The difference between the two pronouns is because the first relative (mā) is explained by "mercy," while the second is unrestricted, encompassing both mercy and wrath. In this there is an indication that His mercy precedes His wrath.

﴿after Him﴾ — after His withholding. ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ — the Overpowering over whatever He wills; none may contest Him in it. ﴿the All-Wise﴾ — He does nothing except with knowledge and perfect precision. Then, when He had made clear that He is the originator of the dominion and the sovereignty and the One who disposes of them both absolutely, He commanded people to be thankful for His favour, saying:

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 3–4:

﴿O people, remember the favour of God upon you﴾ — preserve it by knowing its true worth, acknowledging it, and obeying the One who bestowed it. Then He denied that anyone else has any part in this, such that he would deserve to be associated with Him, by His words: ﴿Is there any creator other than God who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no god but He; so how are you turned away?﴾ — that is, by what means are you diverted from monotheism to associating others with Him? The word (ghayru) [“other than”] is in the nominative (raf‘) to agree with the position (mahall) of ﴿min khaliq﴾ [“any creator”], being either a qualifying attribute (sifah) or a substitute (badal), since the interrogative here carries the sense of negation; or because it is the agent (fa‘il) of ﴿khaliq﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa’i read it in the genitive (jarr), treating it according to its wording (lafz). It has also been read in the accusative (nasb) as an exception (istithna’). The clause ﴿yarzuqukum﴾ [“who provides for you”] is either a qualifying description of ﴿khaliq﴾, or a resumptive clause (isti’naf) explaining it, or an independent statement (kalam mubtada’). On the last view, the wording ﴿Is there any creator﴾ prevents its application to anyone other than God.

﴿And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied﴾ — that is, take them as a model for patience in the face of their denial. He placed ﴿then were denied﴾ in the position of the consequence, dispensing with the mention of the result by mentioning the cause. The indefiniteness of ﴿messengers﴾ serves to magnify them, which calls for greater consolation and encouragement to endure steadfastly.

﴿And to God are all matters returned﴾ — so He will recompense you and them for patience and denial.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 5–6:

﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah﴾ regarding the Gathering (al-hashr) and the recompense. ﴿is true﴾, without any failure in it. ﴿So let not the worldly life delude you﴾, lest the enjoyment of it distract you from seeking the Hereafter and striving for it. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you about Allah﴾, that is, Satan, by making you hope for forgiveness while you persist in disobedience. For although forgiveness is possible, committing sin on the basis of this expectation is like taking poison, relying on the body's ability to expel it. It is also read with a ḍammah (al-ghurūr), and it is either a verbal noun (maṣdar) or a plural, like quʿūd.

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you﴾, a general and ancient enmity. ﴿So take him as an enemy﴾ in your beliefs and your actions, and be on guard against him in all the circumstances of your lives. ﴿He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze﴾: this establishes his enmity and explains his purpose in calling his followers to pursue desire and to incline toward the worldly life.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 7–8:

﴿Those who disbelieve, for them is a severe punishment; and those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ This is a warning to those who answer His call-to-action (du'a) and a promise to those who oppose it, and a cutting-off of empty wishful hopes, and a foundation for the whole matter upon faith and righteous deeds. And His saying:

﴿Is one to whom the evil of his deed is made attractive so that he sees it as good [equal to one who is rightly guided]?﴾ is an affirmation of it (taqrir). That is: Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive, in that his delusion and his desire have overcome his intellect until his judgment was inverted, so that he sees falsehood as truth and ugliness as beauty, like one who has not had it made attractive to him but has been granted success until he recognizes the truth, approves of good deeds, and disapproves of bad deeds as they actually are? The answer is omitted, indicated by: ﴿Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾. It has also been said that its estimated content is: "Is one to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive [such that] your soul would go out after them in regret?" The answer is then omitted, indicated by: ﴿So do not let your soul go out after them in regrets﴾ upon it, and its meaning is: do not destroy yourself, [being consumed] by regrets over them because of their error and their persistence in denial. The three fā' particles are all causal (sababiyyah), except that the first two enter upon the cause and the third enters upon the effect. The plural "regrets" (ḥasarāt) indicates the multiplication of his distress over their states, or the abundance of the blameworthy aspects of their actions, which call for sorrow. And "upon them" (ʿalayhim) is not a complement of it, because the complement of a verbal noun (maṣdar) may not precede it; rather it is a complement of "do not go" (tadhhab), or an explanation of the object of the regret. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾, so He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 9:

﴿And Allah is He who sends the winds﴾. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "al-rih" (the wind) in the singular. ﴿So they stir up clouds﴾ in the narration of the past state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl al-māḍiyah), to bring that wondrous scene to mind, which indicates the perfection of wisdom. And because the purpose is to explain the occurrence of these events with this property, He attributed it to them (the winds). It is also possible that the variation of the verbs is to indicate the continuity of the matter. ﴿Then We drive it to a dead land﴾. Nafi', Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read it with the doubled letter (tashdid, "saddada"; i.e. "suqnahu" with intensive form). ﴿And We revive thereby the earth﴾ with the rain that descends from it. The mention of the clouds is like the mention of the rain, or [it means] by the clouds, for they are the cause of the cause, or [it means] that which becomes rain. ﴿After its death﴾, after its drying out. The shift in both verbs from the third person (ghaybah) to the first person plural is to what is more fitting for exclusivity, because of the greater display of craftsmanship in them. ﴿Thus is the resurrection﴾, i.e., like the reviving of dead land is the resurrection of the dead in the possibility of being brought about, since there is nothing between them except the possibility of a difference in the substance of the analogue, and that has no bearing on it. It has been said regarding the manner of revival that He, exalted is He, sends water from beneath the Throne, from which the bodies of creation will grow.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 10:

﴿Whoever desires honour—﴾ that is, nobility and invincibility. ﴿to Allah belongs all honour﴾; that is, let him seek it from Him, for all of it belongs to Him. Thus he dispenses with the indicator (dalil) by the thing indicated (madlul). ﴿To Him ascend the good word, and the righteous deed raises it up.﴾ This explains by what honour is sought, namely tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) and righteous deeds. Their ascent to Him is a metaphor for His acceptance of them; or it is the ascent of the recording angels with their written pages. The pronoun in ﴿raises it up﴾ refers to ﴿the good word﴾, for deeds are not accepted except with tawhid, and this is supported by the fact that He put ﴿the deed﴾ in the accusative; or it refers to ﴿the deed﴾, for it realizes faith and strengthens it; or it refers to Allah. The specification of this honour for deeds is because of the effort (kulfah) involved in them. It is also read as ﴿yas'adu﴾ in both forms (active and passive), and the one who causes ascent is Allah Most High, or the one who speaks it, or the angel. It has been said that ﴿the good word﴾ includes dhikr, supplication, and recitation of the Qur'an.

And from him, upon him be prayers and peace: "It is: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allah is greatest. When the servant says them, the angel carries them up to the heaven, and they greet with them the Face of the Most Merciful. But if there is no righteous deed, they are not accepted."

﴿And those who plot evil deeds—﴾ the evil plottings; that is, the plottings of the Quraysh against the Prophet, upon him be prayers and peace, in the Dar al-Nadwa (council house), and their deliberating over one of three courses: imprisoning him, killing him, or expelling him. ﴿For them is a severe punishment﴾, which is not regarded as anything compared to what they plot. ﴿And the plotting of those—it will perish﴾; it will be corrupted and will not take effect, because matters are predetermined and do not change by it, as indicated by His saying:

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 11:

﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾ by the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, from it. ﴿Then from a drop of semen﴾ by the creation of his offspring from it. ﴿Then He made you into pairs﴾ males and females. ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾ except with its being known to Him. ﴿And no one is granted a lengthening of life, nor is anything taken from his life﴾ no one whose end is old age has his life extended. ﴿Nor is anything taken from his life﴾ from the life of the one granted a lengthening of life for another, by giving him a life that is shortened from his own life; or, it means that nothing is taken from the life of the one whose life is shortened by making it short. The pronoun refers to him even though he is not mentioned, because its counterpart indicates it, or it refers to the life, with leniency in the expression, relying on the listener's understanding, as in their saying: "Allah does not reward a servant, nor punish him, except with truth." It has also been said that the increase and decrease are in one life, according to different causes recorded in the Preserved Tablet, such as: if Amr performs Hajj, his life will be sixty years, and otherwise forty. It has also been said that what is meant by the decrease is the portion of his life that passes and comes to an end, for it is recorded in the scroll of his life day by day. And it is read by Ya'qub as "wa la yunqisu" in the active voice. ﴿Except that it is in a Book﴾ which is the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, or the Preserved Tablet, or the scroll.

﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾ a reference to the preservation, the increase, or the decrease.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 12:

﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, palatable, pleasant to drink, and that one is salty and bitter.﴾ It is struck as a parable for the believer and the disbeliever. Furat (sweet, that quenches thirst) is the water that quenches thirst; sa'igh (palatable) is that whose descent down the throat is easy; and ujaj (bitter) is that which burns with its saltiness. It is also read sayyigh with shaddah, siygh without shaddah, and milh in the form of fi'l (verb-form).

﴿And from each you eat fresh flesh and extract ornaments which you wear.﴾ This is an digression (istitrad) in describing the two seas and the blessings in them, or it completes the parable. The meaning: just as the two, though they share some benefits, are not alike in that they are not alike in what is intended by water in essence, since what has mixed with one of them has corrupted it and altered it from its perfect natural state, so the believer and the disbeliever are not alike, even if they happen to share some qualities such as courage and generosity, because they differ in the greatest distinguishing feature, which is that one of them remains upon the original natural disposition (fitrah) and the other does not. Or it is a preference of the bitter water over the disbeliever in respect of the benefits it shares with the sweet water. By "ornaments" (ḥilyah) is meant pearls and rubies.

﴿And you see the ships therein﴾ in each. ﴿ploughing﴾ cutting through the water by their passage. ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾ of Allah's bounty, by travelling in them. The lam is connected to "ploughing"; it is also permissible for it to be connected to what the mentioned verbs indicate. ﴿And that you may be thankful﴾ for that. The particle of hope (la'alla) is in regard to what the apparent circumstance requires.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 13–14:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a term appointed.﴾ The "appointed term" is the period of its orbit, or its endpoint, or the Day of Resurrection. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion.﴾ The demonstrative refers to the Agent of these things. (In it is an indication that His being the Agent of them necessitates the establishment of the successive attributes, and it is possible that "to Him belongs the dominion" is an independent statement in the Qur'an.) ﴿And those you call upon besides Him do not possess even a thin membrane of a date-stone (qitmir).﴾ This serves to demonstrate His exclusive possession of divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah). Al-qitmir is the thin covering of the date-stone (nawah).

﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call﴾ because they are inanimate objects. ﴿And even if they heard﴾ hypothetically, ﴿they would not respond to you.﴾ due to their lack of ability to benefit, or because they disown you regarding what you ask of them. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association (of them with Allah)﴾ — by your associating them with Him; they will acknowledge its falsehood, or they will say, ﴿You did not used to worship us.﴾ ﴿And none can inform you like one who is Acquainted (khabir).﴾ No informant can inform you of the matter like one who is Acquainted with it, which is Allah, glorified and exalted is He, for He is the One truly Acquainted with it, unlike all other informants. The intent is to confirm what He has informed of the condition of their gods and to negate what they claim for them.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 15–17:

﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah﴾ in your selves and in what occurs to you. The definite article on "the poor" (al-fuqara') is for emphasis regarding their poverty, as if, because of the intensity of their need and the abundance of their dependence, they are the poor, and the dependence of all other creatures, in comparison with their poverty, is not considered. For this reason He said: ﴿and man was created weak﴾. ﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾, the one who is independent absolutely, the bestower of blessings upon all existing things, such that He deserves praise from them.

﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation﴾, a different people more obedient than you, or another world other than what you know. ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾, not unattainable or hard to achieve.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 18:

﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.﴾ That is, no sinful soul shall bear the sin of another soul. As for His saying: ﴿And they shall surely bear their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾, it refers to the misguided misleaders: they bear the burdens of their misleading others along with the burdens of their own straying, and all of these are their own burdens, with nothing of the burdens of others in them. ﴿And if a heavily laden one calls out﴾ means a soul weighed down by burdens of sin. ﴿For someone to carry some of its load﴾ means to be answered in bearing some of its burdens. ﴿None of it shall be carried﴾ means it will not be answered in bearing anything of it; He denied that its sin could be carried for it, just as He denied that the sin of others could be carried upon it. ﴿Even if he were a near relative﴾ means even if the one called upon were a relative of it. The one called upon is left implicit, because of the indication of ﴿if it calls out﴾ upon him. It is also read as «dhū qurbā» (a near relative), with the predicate omitted, and this is preferable to making kāna (was) a complete verb (kāna al-tāmma), since that does not suit the structure of the sentence. ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾, that is, those who are absent from His punishment, or absent from people in their private moments, or whose punishment is absent from them. ﴿And establish prayer﴾: they are the only ones who benefit from the warning. The difference between the two verbs is due to the continuity mentioned earlier. ﴿And whoever purifies himself﴾ means whoever purifies himself from the defilement of sins. ﴿Only purifies himself for his own self﴾, since its benefit returns to him. It is also read «wa-man azkā fa-innamā yuzakkī» (and whoever purifies, purifies only for himself), and this is a parenthetical emphasis on their fear and their establishing of prayer, since both are part of purification. ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾, so He will recompense them for their purification.

﴿And the blind and the seeing are not alike﴾: the disbeliever and the believer. It is also said that these are two parables, one for the idol and one for God, exalted and majestic is He.

﴿Nor are the darknesses and the light﴾: nor falsehood and truth.

﴿Nor the shade and the scorching heat﴾: nor reward and punishment. The negation of equality is repeated here, "nor" appearing with both parts, to add emphasis. Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 24:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ — meaning: as those who affirm the truth (muhiqqin), or as one who is truthful (muhiqqan); or a sending accompanied by the truth. It is also permissible that it be connected to His saying: ﴿as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾, that is, a bringer of good tidings of the true promise and a warner of the true threat. ﴿And there is not a nation﴾ — people of an era — ﴿but a warner has passed among them﴾ — ﴿خَلا﴾ means "passed on."

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 29–30:

﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾ (who persist in its recitation or in following what is in it, until it became their distinguishing mark and title). By "the Book of Allah" is meant the Qur'an, or the category of Allah's books, in which case it is a commendation of the believers among the (earlier) nations after the account of the state of the deniers. ﴿And establish the prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly﴾ (in whatever manner it happens, without intending either of them specifically). It was said: secrecy applies to the voluntary (sunnah) charity and openness to the obligatory (fard) charity. ﴿Hoping for a commerce﴾ (the attainment of reward through obedience), and this is the predicate of inna. ﴿That will never perish﴾ (will never go slack, and will never be destroyed through loss) is a description of the commerce. And His saying:

﴿That He may pay them their rewards in full﴾ is a cause (ʿillah) of what is implied by it, meaning: decline is removed from it, and it is made to prosper with Allah, so that He pays them their rewards for their deeds through its increase; or it is a cause of what is implied by what was counted of their compliance, such as "they did that so that He might pay them in full"; or it is a consequence (ʿāqibah) of "hoping" (yarjūna). ﴿And increase them of His bounty﴾ beyond what corresponds to their deeds. ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving﴾ of their lapses. ﴿Appreciative﴾ of their acts of obedience, that is, He rewards them for them. This is a cause of the paying in full and the increase, or it is the predicate of inna, and "hoping" (yarjūna) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the waw of "and spent" (anfaqū).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 31:

﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book﴾ means the Qur'an. The particle (min) here is either for explanation (tabyin) or for genus (jins), and the (min) in the phrase is for partition (tab'id).

﴿is the truth, confirming what is before it﴾: "Ahaqquhu" (it is the truth) is a confirming circumstantial clause (hal mu'akkidah), because its being true (haqqiyyatuhu) necessitates its agreement with the heavenly books that preceded it in matters of belief and the fundamentals of the rulings (usul al-ahkam).

﴿Indeed, Allah is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾: He is knowing of the inner and outer states. So if there were in your circumstances anything contrary to prophethood, He would not have revealed to you a book like this one, the inimitable (mu'jiz) Book that is the criterion (ʿiyar) over all other books. The mention of "Acquainted" (khabir) before "Seeing" (basir) indicates that the principal concern in this matter is the spiritual affairs (al-umur al-ruhaniyyah).

Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We chose from among Our servants. Some of them wrong themselves, some are moderate, and some race ahead in good deeds by Allah's permission. That is the great bounty.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 32:

﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book﴾ We decreed its inheritance for you (O Muhammad), or "We shall cause it to inherit," and he expressed it in the past tense because its occurrence is certain. Or it means We caused the earlier nations to inherit it. The conjunction is with ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾ and ﴿And that which We have revealed to you﴾ is a parenthetical clause explaining the manner of the inheritance. ﴿Those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾ means the scholars of the Community, from among the Companions and those who came after them, or the Community as a whole, for Allah has chosen them over all other nations. ﴿Some of them wrong themselves﴾ through falling short in acting upon it. ﴿And some of them are moderate﴾ who act upon it for most of the time. ﴿And some of them race ahead in good deeds by Allah's permission﴾ by combining teaching and guidance with action. It has also been said: the one who wrongs himself is the ignorant, the moderate is the learner, and the one who races ahead is the scholar. It has also been said: the one who wrongs himself is the sinner, the moderate is the one who mixed good with bad, and the one who races ahead is the one whose good deeds outweighed such that his bad deeds were expiated, and this is the meaning of his statement, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him: "As for those who raced ahead, they will enter Paradise and be provided therein without reckoning. As for those who were moderate, they will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for those who wronged themselves, they will be held back for a long time at the Gathering, then Allah will receive them with His mercy."

It has also been said: the one who wrongs himself is the disbeliever, with the pronoun referring to the servants, and the reason for placing it first is the great number of wrongdoers, and because wrongdoing in the sense of ignorance and inclination toward desire is what the natural disposition requires, while moderation and precedence are accidental qualities. ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ refers to the inheritance, or to the choosing, or to the precedence.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 33–35:

﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, they will enter them﴾. It is a subject and predicate (mubtada' and khabar), and the pronoun (in "they will enter them") refers to the three groups, or to "those who" (alladhina), or to the "moderate one" (muqtasid) and the "foremost one" (sabiq), since what is meant by both of them is the category (jins). It is also read as "jannata 'adnin" and "jannati 'adnin", in which case it is in the accusative, governed by a verb implied by the apparent word that explains it. Abu 'Amr read "yudkhalunaha" in the passive form (al-bina' lil-maf'ul). ﴿They will be adorned therein﴾ is a second predicate (khabar thani) or a anticipated circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah). It is also read "yuhallawna" from "halayat al-mar'ah", in which case the form is "halyah" (adornment). ﴿with bracelets of gold﴾: the first "min" (min) is partitive (lil-tab'id) and the second is explanatory (lil-tabyin). ﴿and pearls﴾ is conjoined to "gold" (dhahab), meaning "of gold" set with pearls, or "of gold" in the brilliance of pearls. Nafi' and 'Asim, may God have mercy on them both, read it in the accusative, as a conjunction to the place (mahall) of ﴿min asawira﴾. ﴿And their clothing therein is silk﴾.

﴿And they will say: "Praise be to God, who has removed from us the grief"﴾: their grief over fear of the outcome, or their grief over livelihood and its calamities, or over the whisperings of Iblis and others. It is also read "al-huzn". ("Indeed our Lord is Forgiving") to the sinners, ﴿Appreciative﴾ of the obedient.

﴿He who has settled us in the abode of permanence﴾, i.e., the abode of residence (dar al-iqamah). ﴿By His bounty﴾: by His favor and grace, since nothing is obligatory upon Him. ﴿No fatigue touches us therein﴾: toil (nasab). ﴿Nor does weariness touch us therein﴾: exhaustion (kalal), since there is no obligation therein and no hardship. He followed the negation of toil with the negation of what follows it, for emphasis (mubalaghah).

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 36–37:**

﴿And those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed upon them﴾ — it is not decreed for them to die a second death. ﴿So that they would die﴾ — so that they would find rest. Its accusative form is due to an implied *an* (idmar, an elided particle), and it is recited as *"fa-yamutuna"* (with nominative ending) by way of coordination (ʿatf) with *yuqda* (it is decreed), like His saying: ﴿and they will not be given leave, so that they may make excuses﴾. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ — rather, whenever it subsides, its blaze is increased. ﴿Thus﴾ — like that recompense. ﴿We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ — one who exaggerates in disbelief (kufr) or in ingratitude (kufran). Abu ʿAmr recited *"yujza"* in the passive form, with *kull* (every) as its subject, and it is also recited as *"yujazi"*.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — they will seek help. It is of the form *yafta'iluna*, from *al-sarakh*, which is shouting; it has come to be used for seeking help, because the one seeking help raises his voice. ﴿Our Lord, bring us out, and we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ — with an implied verb of speech, and the restriction of the righteous deed by the stated attribute expresses regret over what they did of other than righteousness, and their acknowledgment of it, and it indicates that their being brought out is for making amends for it, and that they used to think it was righteous, but now the opposite has become clear to them. ﴿Did We not give you lives long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein, and the warner came to you?﴾ — this is a reply from God and a rebuke to them. The phrase *"ma yatadhakkaru fihi"* (long enough for taking heed) encompasses every lifespan in which the accountable person is enabled to reflect and take heed. It has been said that it refers to the span between twenty and sixty years.

It is related from him, peace and blessings be upon him (ﷺ): "The lifespan within which God has left no excuse for the son of Adam is sixty years." The conjunction (ʿatf) is upon the meaning of ﴿Did We not give you lives long enough﴾, for it is for affirmation (taqrir), as if He had said: "We gave you lives long enough, and the warner came to you." The warner is the Prophet (ﷺ) or the Book. It has been said that it is reason, or white hair, or the death of relatives. ﴿So taste [it], for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ — none who would repel the punishment from them.

**Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 36–37:**

﴿And those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed upon them﴾ — it is not decreed for them to die a second death. ﴿So that they would die﴾ — so that they would find rest. Its accusative form is due to an implied *an* (idmar, an elided particle), and it is recited as *"fa-yamutuna"* (with nominative ending) by way of coordination (ʿatf) with *yuqda* (it is decreed), like His saying: ﴿and they will not be given leave, so that they may make excuses﴾. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾ — rather, whenever it subsides, its blaze is increased. ﴿Thus﴾ — like that recompense. ﴿We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ — one who exaggerates in disbelief (kufr) or in ingratitude (kufran). Abu ʿAmr recited *"yujza"* in the passive form, with *kull* (every) as its subject, and it is also recited as *"yujazi"*.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — they will seek help. It is of the form *yafta'iluna*, from *al-sarakh*, which is shouting; it has come to be used for seeking help, because the one seeking help raises his voice. ﴿Our Lord, bring us out, and we will do righteous deeds, other than what we used to do﴾ — with an implied verb of speech, and the restriction of the righteous deed by the stated attribute expresses regret over what they did of other than righteousness, and their acknowledgment of it, and it indicates that their being brought out is for making amends for it, and that they used to think it was righteous, but now the opposite has become clear to them. ﴿Did We not give you lives long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed therein, and the warner came to you?﴾ — this is a reply from God and a rebuke to them. The phrase *"ma yatadhakkaru fihi"* (long enough for taking heed) encompasses every lifespan in which the accountable person is enabled to reflect and take heed. It has been said that it refers to the span between twenty and sixty years.

It is related from him, peace and blessings be upon him (ﷺ): "The lifespan within which God has left no excuse for the son of Adam is sixty years." The conjunction (ʿatf) is upon the meaning of ﴿Did We not give you lives long enough﴾, for it is for affirmation (taqrir), as if He had said: "We gave you lives long enough, and the warner came to you." The warner is the Prophet (ﷺ) or the Book. It has been said that it is reason, or white hair, or the death of relatives. ﴿So taste [it], for the wrongdoers have no helper﴾ — none who would repel the punishment from them.

Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Nothing of it is hidden from Him, so their states are not hidden from Him either. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾: this is a justification for the preceding statement, since whoever knows the concealed contents of the breasts, which are the most hidden of things, is all the more knowing of other things.

﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾: He has handed over to you the keys of disposal over it. It has also been said that "khala'if" means successors one after another, being the plural of khalifah, and that "khulafa'" is the plural of khalif.

﴿So whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾: that is, the recompense for his disbelief.

﴿And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in their Lord except in abhorrence, and their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss﴾: this is an explanation of the preceding statement. The repetition serves to indicate that the disbelief's requirement of each of the two matters independently necessitates its ugliness and the obligation to avoid it. By "maqt" (abhorrence, i.e. the most intense hatred) is meant the abhorrence of Allah, and by "khasar" (loss) is meant the loss of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 40:

﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah?﴾ He means their gods (ālihatahum). The attribution to them is because they made them partners of Allah, or because of what they (the idolaters) possess (lit. "for themselves, regarding what they own").

﴿Show me what they have created of the earth﴾ is a substitution (badal) from (ara'aytum), a substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal), because it has the meaning of "inform me" (akhbirūnī), as if he said: "Inform me about these partners. Show me what part of the earth they have independently created."

﴿Or have they a partnership in the heavens?﴾ Or do they have a partnership with Allah in the creation of the heavens, so that they deserve thereby a partnership in divinity (uluhiyya) in essence?

﴿Or have We given them a Book﴾ speaking in support of our having taken them as partners?

﴿So they are upon clear proof from it﴾ upon evidence from that Book that they have a partnership by appointment (ja'liyya). It is also permissible that the pronoun (hum) refers to the polytheists, as in His saying: ﴿Or have We sent down to them any authority?﴾ Nafi', Ibn Amir, Ya'qub, Abu Bakr and al-Kisa'i read (ʿalā bayyinātin, "upon clear proofs"), which indicates that shirk is a grave matter that requires the convergence of many proofs.

﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾. When He negated the kinds of proof in this matter, He turned away from it by mentioning what moved them to it, which is the deception of the predecessors to the successors, or of the leaders to the followers, by claiming that they are intercessors with Allah who will intercede for them through drawing near to Him.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 41:

﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease [to exist/move from their places]﴾. [He holds them] out of aversion to their ceasing, for what is contingent (mumkin) in its state of existence necessarily needs a preserver. Or [the meaning is] that He prevents them from ceasing, because holding back (al-imsak) is a form of preventing (man').
﴿And if they were to cease, none could hold them after Him﴾: none held them [i.e., none holds them] after Allah, or after their ceasing. The clause takes the place of both answers (of the oath and of the condition). The first "min" is extra (za'idah), and the second "min" denotes the starting point (li'l-ibtida').
﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾: in that He holds them, although they were deserving of being crushed to pieces, as He said: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from above it, and the earth splits open﴾.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 42–43:

﴿And they swore by Allah their most earnest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations.﴾ This is because the Quraysh, when it reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, said: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians! If a messenger came to us, we would surely be better guided than any one of the nations," i.e., than any one of the nations, the Jews, the Christians and others, or than the community of which it is said, "It is one of the nations," as a preference for it over others in guidance and uprightness. ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾ meaning Muhammad, upon him be prayers and peace. ﴿It increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ i.e., the warner, or his coming, as a cause. ﴿Except aversion﴾ distancing themselves from the truth.

﴿Arrogance in the land﴾ is a substitute for (nufuran, "aversion"), or an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu). ﴿And evil plotting﴾: its origin is "wa in makarū al-makra al-sayyi'a" (and if they plotted an evil plot), so the qualified noun was omitted, being replaced by its attribute, then "an" with the verb was replaced by the verbal noun, and then it was put in the genitive construction (idafah). Hamzah alone read it with a sukun on the hamzah in continuous recitation (wasl). ﴿And evil plotting does not encompass﴾ i.e., does not surround. ﴿Except its own people﴾, namely the plotter himself.
